questions.q: Where should you download the Python installer from?
options: A random download-manager app that bundles extra software
python.org/downloads — the official Python Software Foundation site
Any third-party site that ranks first in a search engine
It doesn't matter, every source is identical
questions.explain: python.org is the official source, built and signed by the Python Software Foundation itself.

questions.q: What does the "Add python.exe to PATH" checkbox do, and what happens if you skip it?
options: It is checked by default, so this never needs attention
It only affects installation speed
It lets your OS find the word "python" in a terminal; skipping it causes a confusing "not recognized" error later
It installs a second copy of Python; skipping it has no real effect
questions.explain: The checkbox is unchecked by default, and skipping it means the terminal won't recognize the python command.

questions.q: Which command confirms that pip installed correctly?
options: python check pip
pip install confirm
There is no way to check pip from a terminal
pip --version
questions.explain: pip --version prints pip's real version number if the install succeeded.

questions.q: Why does this course recommend the official Python extension from Microsoft in VS Code?
options: It replaces the need to install Python itself
It is required to use any code editor whatsoever
It adds IntelliSense, linting, debugging, and the ability to run Python files directly inside the editor
It is the only extension that can open .py files at all
questions.explain: The official extension adds the core tooling for writing, running, and debugging Python inside VS Code.

questions.q: What problem does a virtual environment solve?
options: It makes Python code run faster than it otherwise would
It is only useful for people working on exactly one project ever
It replaces the need to ever install any packages
A package installed for one project can silently break another project that needs a different version of the same library
questions.explain: A virtual environment isolates each project's installed packages so version conflicts between projects don't happen.
